mathematical_target.exact_field:
transport : ∀ z ∈ stateNeighborhood S C base ε, stateSector S z.1 →
    ∃ τ : PolarPoint → PolarPoint, ∃ q : PolarPoint → ℝ,
      ContDiffOn ℝ 3 τ (annularOpen D) ∧ ContDiffOn ℝ 3 q (annularOpen D) ∧
      MapsTo τ (annularOpen D) (annularOpen D) ∧
      (∀ p, τ (p + (0, Real.pi)) = τ p + (0, Real.pi)) ∧
      Function.Periodic q (0, Real.pi) ∧
      (∀ p, τ (p.1, -p.2) = ((τ p).1, -(τ p).2)) ∧
      (∀ r θ, q (r, -θ) = q (r, θ)) ∧
      (∀ m, ∀ p ∈ referencePhysicalPieceOpen S K m,
        τ p = canonicalCurrentPoint C K z m p ∧
          q p = K.height (C.referenceState, 0) m p / K.height z m (τ p)) ∧
      ∃ C₀ A : ℝ, 0 < C₀ ∧ 0 ≤ A ∧
        (∀ p ∈ annularOpen D, ∀ n : ℕ, n ≤ 2 →
          ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ n q p‖ ≤ C₀ * T.M p.1 ^ A) ∧
        (∀ p ∈ annularOpen D, ∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → n ≤ 2 →
          ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ n τ p‖ ≤ C₀ * T.M p.1 ^ A) ∧
        (∀ p ∈ annularOpen D,
          T.H (τ p).1 / T.H p.1 ≤ C₀ * T.E0 p.1 ^ A) ∧
        (∀ p ∈ annularOpen D,
          T.M (τ p).1 / T.M p.1 ≤ C₀ * T.E0 p.1 ^ A)

conclusion.tau: On each referencePhysicalPieceOpen S K m, the already selected qualitative transport tau equals the literal stored composite K.inverseChart z m ∘ K.chart (C.referenceState,0) m. The composite identity for canonicalCurrentPoint is definitional.
conclusion.q: On the same reference piece, q = h_ref * (abs(planeJacobian G_z) ∘ F_ref) * ((canonicalSource S K z m (fun _ => 1))⁻¹ ∘ F_ref). The inverse-Jacobian identity needed for this formula is already public with geometry-only hypotheses.
conclusion.smallest_remaining_identity_work: One EqOn lemma using the existing inverse-Jacobian theorem and the definition of canonicalSource; approximately 40–70 Lean lines including imports/namespace, comfortably below the requested 100. No new map, inverse, atlas, family, or global extension is chosen.
conclusion.global_transport_not_completed: The formula is an interior identity. Uniform finite-jet bounds, extension across all cuts/roots, and the two H/M transport-ratio bounds remain separate.

exact_definitions.canonicalSource:
def canonicalSource (S : PhysicalSpacesData) (K : CanonicalData S)
    (z : AnnularState S × ℝ) (m : ℕ) (f : PolarPoint → ℝ) (p : PolarPoint) : ℝ :=
  let x := K.inverseChart z m p
  K.height z m x * f x / |planeJacobian (K.chart z m) x|
exact_definitions.canonicalCurrentPoint:
def canonicalCurrentPoint {S : PhysicalSpacesData}
    (C : NonlinearGeometryData S) (K : CanonicalData S)
    (z : AnnularState S × ℝ) (m : ℕ) (y : PolarPoint) : PolarPoint :=
  K.inverseChart z m (K.chart (C.referenceState, 0) m y)
exact_definitions.referenceDomain:
referenceDomain : ∀ m, physicalPieceOpen S K (C.referenceState, 0) m =
    referencePhysicalPieceOpen S K m
exact_definitions.charts:
charts : ∀ z ∈ stateNeighborhood S C base ε, stateSector S z.1 → ∀ m,
    MapsTo (K.chart z m) (physicalPieceOpen S K z m) (canonicalOpen S K m) ∧
    MapsTo (K.inverseChart z m) (canonicalOpen S K m) (physicalPieceOpen S K z m) ∧
    (∀ p ∈ physicalPieceOpen S K z m, K.inverseChart z m (K.chart z m p) = p) ∧
    (∀ p ∈ canonicalOpen S K m, K.chart z m (K.inverseChart z m p) = p) ∧
    ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ (K.chart z m) (physicalPieceOpen S K z m) ∧
    ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ (K.inverseChart z m) (canonicalOpen S K m) ∧
    ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ (K.height z m) (physicalPieceOpen S K z m) ∧
    (∀ p ∈ physicalPieceOpen S K z m,
      0 < K.height z m p ∧ planeJacobian (K.chart z m) p ≠ 0 ∧
      K.chart z m (p + (0, Real.pi)) = K.chart z m p + (0, Real.pi) ∧
      K.height z m (p + (0, Real.pi)) = K.height z m p)
exact_definitions.N04Properties:
def N04Properties (D : ReferenceData) (T : MaterialData) (S : PhysicalSpacesData)
    (C : NonlinearGeometryData S) (L : ReturnCorrectionData S)
    (K : CanonicalData S) (base loss : ℕ) (ε : ℝ) : Prop :=
  let U := stateNeighborhood S C base ε
  CanonicalGeometry D S C K base ε ∧
  CanonicalCutOperatorProperties S C L K base ε ∧
  (∀ s : ℕ, ∃ B : ℝ, 0 < B ∧ ∀ z ∈ U, ∀ m p,
    p ∈ canonicalOpen S K m → ∀ a b : ℕ, a + b ≤ s →
      |mixedDerivative a b (K.potential z m) p| +
      |mixedDerivative a b (K.dividedDifference z m).a p| +
      |mixedDerivative a b (K.dividedDifference z m).b p| +
      |mixedDerivative a b (K.dividedDifference z m).c p| ≤
        B * T.E0 (T.sample (K.cell m)) ^ B *
          (1 + stateGrading S (s + loss) (z.1 - C.referenceState) + |z.2|)) ∧
  CanonicalSourcePairing D S C K base ε

providers.role: Primary geometry-only inverse-Jacobian identity and the actual no-cost absolute-value jet identity.

public_headers.name: n07a_actual_inverseChart_jacobian_abs
public_headers.header:
theorem n07a_actual_inverseChart_jacobian_abs
    {C : NonlinearGeometryData S} {base : ℕ} {ε : ℝ}
    (hgeom : CanonicalGeometry D S C K base ε)
    {z : AnnularState S × ℝ} (hz : z ∈ stateNeighborhood S C base ε)
    (hs : stateSector S z.1) (m : ℕ) {y : PolarPoint}
    (hy : y ∈ canonicalOpen S K m) :
    |planeJacobian (K.inverseChart z m) y| =
      |planeJacobian (K.chart z m) (K.inverseChart z m y)|⁻¹

public_headers.name: n07a_norm_iteratedFDeriv_abs
public_headers.header:
theorem n07a_norm_iteratedFDeriv_abs
    {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
    {f : E → ℝ} {x : E} (hf : ContinuousAt f x) (hne : f x ≠ 0) (n : ℕ) :
    ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ n (fun y => |f y|) x‖ = ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ n f x‖

public_headers.name: n07a_canonicalHeightInverse_eq_sourceFactorInverse
public_headers.header:
theorem n07a_canonicalHeightInverse_eq_sourceFactorInverse
    {C : NonlinearGeometryData S} {L : ReturnCorrectionData S}
    {base loss : ℕ} {ε : ℝ}
    (h04 : N04Properties D T S C L K base loss ε)
    (z : CanonicalGeometry.Parameter S)
    (hz : liftSectorParameter S C z ∈ stateNeighborhood S C base ε)
    (hs : stateSector S (liftSectorParameter S C z).1)
    (m : ℕ) {y : PolarPoint} (hy : y ∈ canonicalOpen S K m) :
    (K.height (liftSectorParameter S C z) m
      (K.inverseChart (liftSectorParameter S C z) m y))⁻¹ =
        n07aCanonicalAtomField D T S C L K .sourceFactorInverse z m y *
          |planeJacobian (K.inverseChart (liftSectorParameter S C z) m) y|

providers.role: Actual two inverse differential identities on the current physical and canonical open pieces, used in the primary public theorem.

public_headers.name: n07a_actualChart_fderiv_inverse
public_headers.header:
theorem n07a_actualChart_fderiv_inverse
    (hgeom : CanonicalGeometry D S C K base ε)
    {z : AnnularState S × ℝ} (hz : z ∈ stateNeighborhood S C base ε)
    (hs : stateSector S z.1) (m : ℕ) {y : PolarPoint}
    (hy : y ∈ canonicalOpen S K m) :
    (fderiv ℝ (K.chart z m) (K.inverseChart z m y)).comp
        (fderiv ℝ (K.inverseChart z m) y) = ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ PolarPoint ∧
      (fderiv ℝ (K.inverseChart z m) y).comp
        (fderiv ℝ (K.chart z m) (K.inverseChart z m y)) =
          ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ PolarPoint

providers.role: Reviewed endpoint inverse supplier. It gives a local inverse and agreement on an actual interior image collar, but is unnecessary for the open-piece formula.

public_headers.name: canonicalChart_exists_smooth_endpointInverse
public_headers.header:
theorem canonicalChart_exists_smooth_endpointInverse
    {D : ReferenceData} {S : PhysicalSpacesData} {C : NonlinearGeometryData S}
    {K : CanonicalData S} {base : ℕ} {ε : ℝ}
    (hK : Blueprint.N04PartA D S C K base ε)
    {z : AnnularState S × ℝ} (hz : z ∈ stateNeighborhood S C base ε)
    (hsector : stateSector S z.1) (m : ℕ) (p : PolarPoint)
    (hp : p ∈ physicalPieceClosed S K z m) :
    ∃ e : OpenPartialHomeomorph PolarPoint PolarPoint,
      (e : PolarPoint → PolarPoint) = K.chart z m ∧ p ∈ e.source ∧
      ContDiffAt ℝ ∞ e.symm (K.chart z m p) ∧
      EqOn e.symm (K.inverseChart z m)
        (K.chart z m '' (physicalPieceOpen S K z m ∩ e.source))

providers.role: Reviewed genuine closed inverse/germ supplier. No fixed reference rectangle is substituted for a moving physical domain.

public_headers.name: canonicalCurrentPoint_closed_inverse_data
public_headers.header:
theorem canonicalCurrentPoint_closed_inverse_data
    {D : ReferenceData} {S : PhysicalSpacesData}
    {C : NonlinearGeometryData S} {K : CanonicalData S} {base : ℕ} {ε : ℝ}
    (hA : CanonicalGeometry D S C K base ε)
    (hz₀ : (C.referenceState, 0) ∈ stateNeighborhood S C base ε)
    (hs₀ : stateSector S C.referenceState)
    {z : AnnularState S × ℝ} (hz : z ∈ stateNeighborhood S C base ε)
    (hs : stateSector S z.1) (k : ℕ) {p : PolarPoint}
    (hp : p ∈ physicalPieceClosed S K (C.referenceState, 0) k) :
    ContDiffAt ℝ ∞ (canonicalReferencePoint C K z k)
        (canonicalCurrentPoint C K z k p) ∧
      canonicalReferencePoint C K z k ∘ canonicalCurrentPoint C K z k =ᶠ[𝓝 p]
        (id : PolarPoint → PolarPoint) ∧
      canonicalCurrentPoint C K z k ∘ canonicalReferencePoint C K z k
        =ᶠ[𝓝 (canonicalCurrentPoint C K z k p)] (id : PolarPoint → PolarPoint)

public_headers.name: canonicalReferenceGauge_reconstructs_closed_fields

        (canonicalReferencePoint C K z m) (n04CoordinatesCurrentHeightRatio C K z m)

theorem n04WholeReferenceGaugeAtlasData_relative_fields_eq
    (z : AnnularState S × ℝ)
    (href : ∀ i, τ (C.referenceState, 0) i = id ∧
      σ (C.referenceState, 0) i = id ∧ Q (C.referenceState, 0) i = (fun _ => 1))
    (hχψ : ∀ i, Function.LeftInverse (χ i) (ψ i))
    (hστ : ∀ i, Function.LeftInverse (σ z i) (τ z i))
    (hh₀ : ∀ i p, h₀ i p ≠ 0) :

    ∀ m, canonicalCurrentPoint C V z m = canonicalCurrentPoint C W z m ∧
      canonicalReferencePoint C V z m = canonicalReferencePoint C W z m ∧

theorem canonicalCurrentHeightRatio_eq_sourceJacobianPullback
    {D : ReferenceData} {S : PhysicalSpacesData}
    {C : NonlinearGeometryData S} {K : CanonicalData S}
    {base : ℕ} {ε : ℝ}
    (hgeom : CanonicalGeometry D S C K base ε)
    (hz₀ : (C.referenceState, 0) ∈ stateNeighborhood S C base ε)
    (hs₀ : stateSector S C.referenceState)
    {z : AnnularState S × ℝ}
    (hz : z ∈ stateNeighborhood S C base ε)
    (hs : stateSector S z.1) (m : ℕ) :
    EqOn
      (fun p => K.height (C.referenceState, 0) m p /
        K.height z m (canonicalCurrentPoint C K z m p))
      (fun p => K.height (C.referenceState, 0) m p *
        |planeJacobian (K.inverseChart z m)
          (K.chart (C.referenceState, 0) m p)| *
        (canonicalSource S K z m (fun _ => 1)

minimal_future_producer.expected_lines: 40–70 including namespace/header and proof; no Lean written in this task
proof_steps: Introduce p and hp from EqOn; construct hp₀, hy, and hx with the exact domain chain above.

Set hc := hgeom.charts z hz hs m. Obtain hh : K.height z m (K.inverseChart z m y) ≠ 0 from (hc.2.2.2.2.2.2.2 _ hx).1.ne'; obtain hj : |planeJacobian (K.chart z m) (K.inverseChart z m y)| ≠ 0 by abs_ne_zero.mpr applied to the same tuple's .2.1.
Use n07a_actual_inverseChart_jacobian_abs hgeom hz hs m hy to rewrite the inverse Jacobian factor.

Inside the proof, establish the same-point scalar identity (K.height z m (K.inverseChart z m y))⁻¹ = |planeJacobian (K.inverseChart z m) y| * (canonicalSource S K z m (fun _ => 1) y)⁻¹. After the public Jacobian rewrite, simp only [canonicalSource, mul_one], then field_simp [hh,hj]. This is the scalar algebra H⁻¹ = J⁻¹*(H/J)⁻¹.

Apply congrArg (fun u : ℝ => K.height (C.referenceState,0) m p * u) to that identity, and normalize with canonicalCurrentPoint, div_eq_mul_inv and mul_assoc. This supplies exactly the proposed RHS ordering.
No theorem for tau is necessary: canonicalCurrentPoint is already definitionally G_z ∘ F_ref.
assumptions_not_added: No final CurrentJets, ReferenceJets, transport bound or material floor is a hypothesis.
No global homeomorphism of total chart functions is asserted.
No equality of current physical pieces with reference rectangles is used for negative pieces.
No new inverse choice and no new reference family is made.

transfer_to_the_selected_global_maps.exact_qualitative_predicate:
def WholeCanonicalTransportQualitative
    {D : ReferenceData} {S : PhysicalSpacesData}
    (C : NonlinearGeometryData S) (W : CanonicalData S)
    (z : AnnularState S × ℝ) (F : PolarPoint → PolarPoint) (q : PolarPoint → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ContDiffOn ℝ 3 F (annularOpen D) ∧ ContDiffOn ℝ 3 q (annularOpen D) ∧
    MapsTo F (annularOpen D) (annularOpen D) ∧
    (∀ p, F (p + (0, Real.pi)) = F p + (0, Real.pi)) ∧
    Function.Periodic q (0, Real.pi) ∧
    (∀ p, F (p.1, -p.2) = ((F p).1, -(F p).2)) ∧
    (∀ r θ, q (r, -θ) = q (r, θ)) ∧
    (∀ m, ∀ p ∈ referencePhysicalPieceOpen S W m,
      F p = canonicalCurrentPoint C W z m p ∧
        q p = W.height (C.referenceState, 0) m p / W.height z m (F p)) ∧
    ∀ p ∈ annularOpen D, 0 < q p
transfer_to_the_selected_global_maps.actual_pointwise_step: For the already chosen global F,q and hqual, its hfields m p hp gives F p = canonicalCurrentPoint C K z m p and q p = href p / hz(F p). Rewrite the latter with the first equality, then apply the EqOn producer at p.
transfer_to_the_selected_global_maps.ordinary_germ_step: referencePhysicalPieceOpen is Ioo × univ and hence open. At p in it, combine its neighborhood membership with the pointwise equality to get eventual equality of the actual global functions with the stated composites/products.
transfer_to_the_selected_global_maps.finite_derivative_step: Use the actual germ to transfer iteratedFDeriv. The public n07a_norm_iteratedFDeriv_abs itself exhibits the pinned EventuallyEq.iteratedFDeriv usage, and CanonicalReferenceGauge_closed_fullJets demonstrates the actual finite-jet germ transfer route. No globally valid total inverse identity is needed.
transfer_to_the_selected_global_maps.no_new_qualitative_selection: Reuse the exact F/q already carried by WholeCanonicalTransportQualitative. The global-transfer theorem is a witness-preserving transfer, not a source of new quantitative constants.

finite_order_budget.required_actual_inputs: G_z positive Frechet jets through 2 at y and F_ref positive jets through 2 at p.
finite_order_budget.zero_order_note: No quantitative G_z or F_ref value norm is needed for positive derivative bounds; actual image membership is required.

finite_order_budget.required_actual_inputs: h_ref jets0..2 at p; F_ref positive jets1..2; G_z positive jets1..3 at y; the literal reciprocal canonicalSource S K z m (fun _=>1) jets0..2 at y.
finite_order_budget.jacobian_reason: The Jacobian is a quadratic expression in DG_z, so two derivatives of it use G_z derivatives up to order3.

finite_order_budget.required_actual_inputs: ContDiffOn of G_z on the true canonical open set and nonvanishing of its Jacobian there.
finite_order_budget.quantitative_note: Local sign constancy transfers derivative norms exactly. This step requires no uniform numerical lower bound for the Jacobian and performs no new quantitative reciprocal estimate.

finite_order_budget.required_actual_inputs: The actual same-K physical and canonical widths and their established costs whenever the input bounds are stated in unit coordinates.
Uniform-in-m constants and the actual same-sample/physical-point comparisons converting input E0 or normalized-weight costs to C0*T.M(p.1)^A.

remaining_global_obligations: Retain the same global C3 transport supplied by the actual whole atlas construction; the local identity alone does not build or prove global C3 matching.
First establish bounds uniform over all reference pieces and the same selected family. Constants depending arbitrarily on a piece cannot be used in CanonicalPrimitiveGeometry.transport.

Extend the uniform n≤2 estimates through cuts and roots using the actual global C3 regularity and a proved coverage/density or endpoint argument. CanonicalGeometry.referencePartition supplies null-exception coverage, but this report does not claim that the needed global extension lemma has been implemented.
Preserve the original source sample and all unit-width factors. The target q/tau estimates use T.M at the reference physical radius, not an arbitrary endpoint or moving-half sample.
Prove T.H((tau p).1)/T.H(p.1) and T.M((tau p).1)/T.M(p.1) against the same reference-point E0 weight. The Jacobian/source identity does not imply these ratios.

For a negative moving piece, tau p lies in the actual current domain. It must not be treated as automatically lying in the corresponding fixed reference half. The separately reviewed ActualNegativeMovingReferenceUnitPoint identifies a genuine old reference half or cut in the same full component, but does not by itself prove a material comparison or the global ratios.

Contains actual source recursions and compact/state-dependent bounds, not the required uniform Stage E material producer.
Its source spatial bounds take numerical geometry bounds as input. It is not a source of those inputs or a replacement for the transport identity.
Provides actual inverse differential/test formulas under stronger h04 assumptions; unnecessary given the geometry-only inverse-Jacobian identity.
